A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TROLL by the same authors. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching material moved between appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original mathematical-reasoning experiments, comparisons across models and training algorithms, hyperparameter analyses, and computational-overhead measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds code-generation experiments, additional algorithm comparisons, batch-size experiments, and code-generation entropy analyses.

M1.justification: The KL projection, dual optimization and differentiation, regression objective, and sparsification procedure are retained. Algorithm 1 and Figure 6 explain the existing procedure. Additional training algorithms use the same projection; the PDFs do not establish a revised TROLL component.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates mathematical reasoning and lists code generation as future work. v2 adds training and evaluation on Eurus-Code, comprising programming tasks from APPS, CodeContests, TACO, and Codeforces. This introduces a distinct task domain requiring executable solutions. Existing math coverage is retained; Eurus-Math is a clarified name for the previous math subset.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 4 and their associated curves add REINFORCE++ comparisons for Qwen3-8B and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. Appendix D.4 and Figure 14 additionally evaluate adaptive clipping through BAPO and clipping-free GPG, including GPG with TROLL. These substantially broaden the comparator set beyond the retained GRPO, Dr.GRPO, PPO, and GSPO comparisons.

E3.justification: New code experiments introduce test-execution rewards, a ten-second timeout, up to ten test cases, and evaluation averaging pass@1 across four benchmarks. Appendix E.2 adds batch sizes from 256 to 2048, increasing updates between data collections. Existing default hyperparameters remain unchanged. The sensitivity caption changes from 8B to 1.7B, but Section 6 still says 8B, so a rerun is not established.

E4.justification: Appendix E.2 and Figure 16 add a controlled batch-size study testing robustness to increasingly stale rollout data. Figure 17 adds entropy-versus-success analysis across Qwen3 sizes on code generation. These extend the stability and behavioral analyses substantially. Earlier KL/sparsity sensitivity, overhead, response-length analyses, and example generations remain present after relocation.

E5.justification: Both versions retain 32-response averaging for AMC and AIME evaluations and the same sliding-window smoothing with unsmoothed curves displayed. Neither reports training-seed counts, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The new plots do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds code-generation results, reporting 7–18 percentage-point advantages over Clip, plus REINFORCE++, BAPO/GPG, batch-size, and entropy findings. For example, new Qwen3-8B REINFORCE++ DAPO-Eval entries are 0.626 for Clip and 0.728 for TROLL. These are newly reported comparisons. All retained numerical entries in Tables 1, 4, and 5 match v1.

T1.justification: Equation 4 restores a missing logarithm on the current-policy probability, Equation 8 corrects the Lagrangian expansion, and Appendix A.3 revises multiplier signs around the KKT expressions. These are local mathematical corrections. The sparsification theorems, assumptions, and bounds are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain differentiable categorical trust-region projections, scalable sparsification, and improved training relative to clipping. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion now explicitly extend the demonstrated benefits to code generation, including a new quantitative code-performance claim. Code generation was previously future work.

C2.justification: v2 interprets batch-size results as evidence that projection tolerates older rollout data and explains GPG stabilization through constraining policy outputs without requiring importance ratios. It also connects code-generation performance with entropy preservation. Code generation leaves the future-work discussion; limitations concerning larger models, mixture-of-experts architectures, and other modalities remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds the overall training pseudocode and documents Eurus-Code filtering, sample counts, reward execution, PRIME reward management, and SandboxFusion. The project-link footnote now advertises datasets as well as code. However, the unchanged reproducibility statement still promises future release, leaving actual availability unresolved. Existing solver listings, checkpoints, default hyperparameters, and hardware information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially broadens positioning against adaptive clipping, expected-KL regularization, clipping-free policy gradients, Q-learning, and contrastive/off-policy approaches. New references include BAPO, GPG, REINFORCE++, MPO, and several alternative LLM reinforcement-learning methods. This expands the comparison landscape beyond the earlier emphasis on PPO-style algorithms and Gaussian trust-region projections.

P1.justification: The introduction and related work are extensively rewritten, and the method explanation gains named stages and reordered discussion of optimization and differentiation. Analysis becomes a separate main section, while appendix analyses are reorganized into Appendix E and unchanged example generations move to Appendix F. Terminology, notation, and publication headers are also revised.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 3 gain code-generation panels; Tables 1 and 4 and associated plots gain REINFORCE++ comparisons. v2 adds Algorithm 1, the computation graph in Figure 6, and Figures 14, 16, and 17 for new comparisons and analyses. Multiple retained displays are resized, relocated, or given revised captions and legends.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for TROLL's generality and stability: code generation moves from future work to experiments across model sizes, while BAPO/GPG comparisons and the batch-size study test alternatives and operating conditions absent from v1. Training pseudocode, the computation graph, and local mathematical corrections improve clarity. Seed-level uncertainty remains unreported, but the additions address important limits of the earlier empirical validation.
